intro: These crops come from Polish-language newspapers printed in the United States between the 1880s and the 1940s, held by the Library of Congress. Keep the marks on letters (ą ć ę ł ń ó ś ź ż) as printed, and old spellings.
name: Polish: type the crops
rules: Type each printed line on its own line, in reading order. Keep the printed spelling, capital letters, punctuation and hyphens, even where they look wrong, and don't join a word split across lines. If the crop cuts a line at its edge, type only the letters wholly inside it. Where you can't read a letter or a stretch of letters, press the button that inserts � instead of guessing. If nothing at all is legible, press Nothing legible. Two people type each one independently. If they differ, a third person compares both with the print and settles it. A few items have a known text that checks your typing.
title: Polish: type the crops
